questions.question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

“Mrs. Pooja is / very busy at / the moment.” / “All right. I had been waiting.”
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "All right. I had been waiting".

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence that contains a grammatical error is 'All right. I had been waiting'.
 
• The word 'had been' is used to mean that **something happened in the past and has already ended**.
 
 
• *Example: I had been working at the company for five years when I got the promotion.*
 
 
 
• Whereas the word 'will be' is used **to refer to actions that will be happening in the future.**
 
 
• *​Example: The Spider-Man movie will be releasing soon.​*
 
 
 
• Therefore, the use of 'had been' in the sentence should be replaced with 'will be' to make it grammatically correct.

 

Correct sentence__: *"**Mrs. Pooja is very busy at the moment.” “All right. I **will be **waiting."*

questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.

She blew the candles on the cake.

options.text: The candles on the cake were blew by her.
The candles on the cake were blown by her.
The candles on the cake were being blown by her.
The candles on the cake is blown by her.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'The candles on the cake were blown by her.'

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is in Past Tense and in Active Voice.
 
• The rule for changing a sentence in Past Tense from Active voice to Passive voice:
 
 
• Interchange the object and subject with each other, i.e. object of the active sentence become the subject of the passive sentence.
 
• The helping verb comes before the object in the passive voice as the passive voice starts with the object of the active voice.
 
• Convert the verb into past participle or 3rd form of the verb.
 
• Structure: Subject + V2 + object (Active Voice)__
 
 

 Object + was/were + V3 + by + Subject __(Passive Voice)__ 

__
 
• Solution: *She blew the candles on the cake. *(Active Voice)

 * The candles on the cake were blown by her. *(Passive Voice)

 
• Therefore, the correct answer is 'The candles on the cake were blown by her.'

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• In Active Voice, a sentence emphasizes the subject performing an action.
 
• In Passive Voice, the sentence emphasizes the action or the object of the sentence.
 
 
• Example: *He reads a novel. *(Active Voice)

 * A novel is read by him. *(Passive Voice)
